title: Latin radio on WLIB and Joe Loco at the Apollo
summary: McRae persuaded a deejay to play Latin music and Joe Loco broke up the Apollo, while booker Teddy Powell controlled Newark.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So I says, "I wanna take you to Newark." Now, while (inaudible) I had this Concert In Jam,
I brought -- the fella says --
One of the bookers, Teddy Powell had Newark sewed up, so I couldn't buck him because he had everything tied up.
So I was in --
So I told him, I say, "I'm taking Joe Loco to Newark on a Monday night." So I took Joe Loco -- brought Joe Loco in one Monday night.
And all the kids found out that Joe Loco was coming over that Monday night. They were all in the street and everywhere.
Packed! Biggest crowd I ever had there.
So now, I go to Schiffman, I say, "Look, I got a star."
Say, "I wanna bring Joe Loco. You know, the Latin people would come (inaudible) to the Apollo."
At that time, I had told Jack Walker on WLIB -- I say, "Look, why don't you -- these Latin guys I'm booking -- Tito Puente, Tito Rodriguez," because those guys are popular.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I say, "Why don't you give them fifteen minutes, you know, play some latin music." And he took --
And Jack Walker and I -- I'm going to (inaudible) tell him something and it sound good to him, he say, "Yeah, I think I'll try that out."
So I brought him Joe Loco records and Tito Puente records. So he played fifteen minutes and (inaudible).
The Latin people started calling in and "Hey, great!" You know, give them more time, you know.

In the meanwhile, I talked to Schiffman about bringing Joe Loco in the Apollo Theater. So he says, "Wait a minute, you want fifteen hundred dollars for this act." He say, "I'll give you twelve." And if he's good as you say he is, I'll give you the balance of the fifteen hundred you want (inaudible)."
I say, "Okay."
I brought Joe Loco in the theater, and the first show he broke it up. Every show. Latin people coming from all over, you know. Broke it up.
And after the first show, I was coming
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
to see. out (inaudible) -- Schiffman (inaudible). He say, "Oh, don't worry about it, you got your fifteen-sixteen hundred. Don't worry about it."
And I was really successful with Joe Loco. I made him more money (than inaudible) Schiffman -- Arnold Shaw Agency.
